articles.headline: Security Slam 2026 – Fall edition: CNCF’s new OpenSSF partnership drops a ready‑to‑use security library
articles.dek: The CNCF teams up with the Open Source Security Foundation for the sixth Security Slam, delivering a curated library of vetted policies for platform engineers.

body.text: Key Takeaway

CNCF’s Security Slam returns for its sixth fall edition and now partners with the Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) to ship a curated “Slam Library” of vetted security policies [FACT:8962c7bb853049be6c524bf81a35d8d4][FACT:b8ea771a2571e647c0f992639ec7325d]. The library is maintained by OpenSSF project leads and a core group of trusted maintainers, giving you confidence the checks aren’t experimental code [FACT:9cdcb418ca7a6159d1aeb2c2864246cc].
Why This Matters

Platform engineers can import the library directly into CI pipelines, shaving weeks off the time it normally takes to source, vet, and test security rules [FACT:3aca8af5a22aa1aa1a768a88ac2b6216]. Because the policies are backed by the CNCF community effort, they stay aligned with the latest Kubernetes hardening best practices [FACT:df849bb2ec0a6070da0a5cc125364cf7].
What Happened

The event kicks off on 2026‑09‑25, with registration open now and a dedicated CNCF booth #313 at KubeCon where the Slam Library will be demoed [FACT:150f468439200b820992a9552c94fc87][FACT:e868ad68a1f59d0ad5a34119167d8bb0][FACT:bdcd7b78eb441118b3411a4ede908f52].
Builder View

Sign up via the CNCF page, pull the ‘slam‑library’ container image, and run it against a test cluster to surface misconfigurations before they hit production [FACT:e868ad68a1f59d0ad5a34119167d8bb0][FACT:9cdcb418ca7a6159d1aeb2c2864246cc]. The library’s policy bundles work out‑of‑the‑box with tools like OPA, Kyverno, and Open Policy Agent gatekeepers, so you can drop them into existing pipelines with minimal friction [FACT:3aca8af5a22aa1aa1a768a88ac2b6216].
Open Questions

Documentation for niche integrations (e.g., service‑mesh policy checks) is still a work in progress, and the CNCF has not announced the exact cadence for future Slam Library releases [FACT:df849bb2ec0a6070da0a5cc125364cf7].
Ardur Take

With six consecutive editions, an official OpenSSF partnership, and maintainers from the core security projects, the Security Slam offers a high‑confidence, low‑risk way to harden your clusters this quarter [FACT:8962c7bb853049be6c524bf81a35d8d4][FACT:b8ea771a2571e647c0f992639ec7325d][FACT:9cdcb418ca7a6159d1aeb2c2864246cc].

articles.headline: Pentagon’s Anthropic supply‑chain risk label survives appeal, court says
articles.dek: A federal appeals court upheld the Department of Defense’s decision to label Anthropic a national‑security supply‑chain risk, confirming the agency’s authority to flag commercial AI providers.

body.text: Key Takeaway

The 9th Circuit affirmed the Pentagon’s “supply‑chain risk” designation for Anthropic, meaning the government can formally flag commercial AI firms as security concerns [FACT:a2c9238f9917f7598087d77cc0bda931][FACT:3741fc758238049806b1ccb5ea05fa8a].
Why This Matters

For builders, the ruling translates into extra compliance steps: contracts that reference Anthropic’s Claude models may need new vetting, and some procurement pipelines could be blocked until the company addresses the label [FACT:a2c9238f9917f7598087d77cc0bda931].
What Happened

On Sept 25‑26 2026, the appeals court issued an opinion that upheld the Pentagon’s earlier move to label Anthropic a supply‑chain risk, a decision reported by multiple outlets including WQOW, Le Monde, and CBS [FACT:a2c9238f9917f7598087d77cc0bda931][FACT:3a320791913bb88a5305e6d6d18b392f].
Builder View

If your stack relies on Claude‑2 or Claude‑3, expect the department to demand security assessments, possible contract pauses, and perhaps higher licensing fees; Anthropic has already warned the label costs the company billions [FACT:5fae6cf40aad32209be3c298bf5090d4].
Open Questions

The court’s opinion does not set a timeline for how long the risk label remains in force, nor does it outline a remediation pathway, leaving those details to future Pentagon guidance [FACT:a2c9238f9917f7598087d77cc0bda931].
Ardur Take

Multiple independent reports confirm the appellate ruling and the Pentagon’s authority, giving us high confidence that this policy will stick and that other AI vendors could face similar designations [FACT:a2c9238f9917f7598087d77cc0bda931][FACT:3a320791913bb88a5305e6d6d18b392f].

Anthropic says the label has already cost it billions in operational impact [FACT:5fae6cf40aad32209be3c298bf5090d4]
